chunks: 8 - My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa narrated to us from Musa b. al-Qasim al-Bajali from Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Sama'a from 'Abdullah b. Muskan from al-Hakam b. al-Salt from Abi Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

Take hold of the belt of this bald man — meaning 'Ali — for indeed he is the Great Truthful One (al-Siddiq al-Akbar), and he is the Distinguisher (al-Faruq) who distinguishes between truth and falsehood. Whoever loves him, Allah guides him; whoever hates him, Allah hates him; and whoever opposes him, Allah destroys him. From him are the two clans of my nation — al-Hasan and al-Husayn — and they are my two sons. From al-Husayn are the Imams of Guidance; Allah has granted them my knowledge and my understanding. So align yourselves with them and do not take a confidant from besides them, lest the wrath of your Lord come upon you. And whoever upon whom the wrath of his Lord comes has indeed fallen. And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of vanity (1).

key_terms.أَئِمَّة الْهُدَى: A'immat al-Huda - Imams of Guidance: the divinely appointed leaders descending from al-Husayn
key_terms.الصِّدِّيق الْأَكْبَر: al-Siddiq al-Akbar - the Great Truthful One: a title bestowed by the Prophet on Imam Ali, signifying supreme truthfulness
key_terms.الفَارُوق: al-Faruq - the Distinguisher: one who distinguishes between truth and falsehood, a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.سِبْط: Sibt - clan/grandchild: refers to al-Hasan and al-Husayn as the two distinguished branches of the Prophet's nation
key_terms.وَلِيجَة: Walija - confidant/intimate protector: one taken as a trusted ally, cautioning against allegiance to others besides the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What titles did Prophet Muhammad give to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition narrated through Imam al-Baqir (as) from his forefathers, the Prophet Muhammad (s) exhorts the Muslim community to cling to Imam Ali (as), bestowing upon him the titles al-Siddiq al-Akbar (the Great Truthful One) and al-Faruq (the Distinguisher between truth and falsehood). The Prophet declares that those who love Ali will be guided by Allah, those who hate him will incur divine wrath, and those who oppose him will be destroyed. He identifies al-Hasan and al-Husayn as the two distinguished branches of his nation and his own sons, and states that the Imams of Guidance descend from al-Husayn, having been granted divine knowledge and understanding. The hadith concludes with a Quranic echo (3:185) warning that worldly life is nothing but the enjoyment of vanity.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa narrated to us from Musa b. al-Qasim al-Bajali from Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Sama`a from `Abdullah b. Muskan from al-Hakam b. al-Salt from Abi Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:

Take to the belt of this bald man (al-anza`) – meaning, `Ali – for he is the Great Saint (al-siddiq al-akbar), and he is the Distinguisher (al-faruq) who will distinguish between truth and falsehood. He who loves him is guided by Allah, he who hates him is hated by Allah, and he who opposes him is destroyed by Allah. From him are the clans of my Nation – al-Hasan and al-Husayn – and they are my sons. The Imams of Guidance are from al-Husayn. Allah has granted them my knowledge and my understanding. So, align with them, and do not take refuge with other than them, or else the wrath of your Lord will come upon you. He whose Lord’s wrath comes upon him has fallen. The life of this world is not but the enjoyment of vanity.
